1

Land owner is in appeal aggrieved of order dated 28.03.2016 passed by the Reference Court,
whereby reference application filed under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'the 1894 Act'), for setting aside order dated 03.08.2012, whereby LAC case was dismissed in default, stands rejected holding that the same was barred by limitation.
2
It is not in dispute that the land of the appellant stands acquired by State.
Award was passed.
Feeling dissatisfied by the award, application under Section 18 of the 1894 Act was filed which was referred to the Reference Court.
The same was dismissed in default on 03.08.2012.
Application under Order 9 Rule 9 CPC seeking restoration of the reference was filed accompanied by an application seeking condonation of delay of about 2 years.

sentences.text: Reference Court dismissed the same holding that in view of Article 122 of the Limitation Act, 1963 (for short 'the 1963 Act') limitation prescribed was 30 days.
4 Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the delay caused was neither intentional nor deliberate as the appellant never received any notice from the Reference Court.
The appellant is an old man.

After he came to know of the dismissal of the reference immediately present application under Order 9 Rule 9 CPC was moved accompanied by an application seeking condonation of delay for 5 Per contra learned State counsel refers to the impugned order and submits that the Reference Court rightly found that the reasons mentioned in the application seeking restoration were unconvincing.

Application was filed after delay of more than two years and thus the Reference Court rightly declined the application filed under Order 9 Rule 9 CPC and the reason assigned by the appellant is falsified from the fact that the counsel was earlier appearing for many dates.
6 I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the records of the case.

7 Leave aside the question of limitation in preferring application seeking restoration of reference,
the reference Court erred in dismissing reference petition for default.
The reference Court is under statutory obligation to answer the reference and has no jurisdiction to dismiss the same for non-prosecution.
Reference can be made to law poova sHarma laid down by Supreme Court in Khazan SIngh (dead) by LRs.

Vs. 2025 PHA Oo aoe FAO-795-2017 (O&M) 3 Union of India, 2002 (2) RCR (Civil) 69 (SO observing as under :-
"4.

Section 18 of the Act empowers a person interested in the land to move by a written application to the Collector requiring that the matter be referred for determination of the Court, whether his objection be to the measurement of the land,
the amount of compensation, the person to whom it is payable, or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested. If the application for reference is in order the Collector is bound to make a reference of it to the Court. Section 20 of the Act enjoins on the Court to "proceed to determine the objection".
The Court shall after holding such inquiry as may be necessary pass an award.

Section 26 of the Act reads thus:
"26. Form of Awards.-(1) Every award under this Part shall be in writing signed by the Judge, and shall specify the amount awarded under clause first of sub-section (1)
of Section 23, and also the amounts (if any) respectively awarded under each of the other clauses of the same sub- section, together with the grounds of awarding each of the said amounts.
(2) Every such award shall be deemed to be a decree and the statement of the grounds of every such award a judgment within the meaning of Section 2, clause (2)
and Section 2, clause (9), respectively, of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908."

sentences.text: The provisions above subsumed would thus make it clear that the Civil Court has to pass an award in answer to the reference made by the Collector under Section 18 of the Act.

If any party to whom notice has been served by the Civil Court did not participate in the inquiry it would only be at his risk because an award would be passed perhaps to the detriment of the concerned party.
But non-participation of any party would not confer jurisdiction on the Civil Court to dismiss the reference for default."

8 Apart from above, there can not be any dispute with respect to the fact that the limitation prescribed for filing application for POOJA SHARMA 2028: PH aciassa # FAO-795-2017 (O&M) 4 restoration would be governed by Article 122 of the 1963 Act.
9 The limitation is fatal to the case only where there is a third party right created.
Here is a case wherein the land owner is seeking compensation in terms of Section 23 of the 1894 Act.
In terms of proviso appended to Article 31 A of the Constitution of India, State is under bounden duty to pay compensation to the land owner as per the market price.
Section 23 of the 1894 Act only embodies the same.

Right to property being a constitutional right guaranteed under Article 300 A of the Constitution of India, this Court finds that the Reference Court instead of dismissing the application seeking condonation of delay ought to have allowed the applications filed by the appellant seeking restoration of the reference and decide the same accordingly.

Needless to observe the intention of the legislature has been well laid down under Section 28(A) of the 1894 Act wherein the land owner who has not even preferred the reference is entitled to the same compensation as has been awarded to the similarly situated land owners.
Finding that the impugned order passed by the Reference Court is not sustainable in the eyes of law, the same is hereby ordered to be quashed.
11 Reference preferred by the appellant is ordered to be restored to its original number.
The appellant is directed to appear before the Reference Court on 04.02.2025.
Reference Court shall make an endavour to answer reference expeditiously considering that the same is pending since the year 2011.
